message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.12","text":"But if someone should wish to say that foreknowledge through such predictions is similar to genuinely innate foreknowledge, that person is greatly deceived. For such things disclose only what is present—and even that only if they speak truth. Yet in another respect even these are useful to me, for they establish that foreknowledge exists. But the foreknowledge of the one true prophet not only knows what is present but also extends its prophecy without limit as far as the future age itself, and it needs no one for comprehension; and, of prophecies, obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things—just as our teacher, being also a prophet, knew all things at all times through an innate and ever-flowing spirit.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν διὰ τῶν τοιούτων προρρήσεων","chosen":"foreknowledge through such predictions","rationale":"The feminine article introduces an implied noun, most naturally πρόγνωσις from the immediate context."},{"source_quote":"ἄλλως δέ μοι καὶ αὐτὰ εὐχρηστεῖ","chosen":"Yet in another respect even these are useful to me","rationale":"ἄλλως marks another respect in which such predictions assist the argument despite not constituting genuine innate foreknowledge."},{"source_quote":"ἡ δὲ τοῦ μόνου καὶ ἀληθοῦς πρόγνωσις","chosen":"But the foreknowledge of the one true prophet","rationale":"“Prophet” is supplied from the surrounding discussion of the true prophet and from the closing description of the teacher as a prophet. A more formally literal alternative is “the foreknowledge of the sole and true one.”"},{"source_quote":"μέχρις αὐτοῦ τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος ἀπέραντον ἐκτείνει τὴν προφητείαν","chosen":"extends its prophecy without limit as far as the future age itself","rationale":"ἀπέραντον characterizes the prophecy as unlimited, while μέχρις marks its reach as extending to the future age itself."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὐδενὸς δεῖται πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν","chosen":"and it needs no one for comprehension","rationale":"The masculine sense “no one” is favored by the subsequent mention of another prophet. The neuter alternative, “it needs nothing for comprehension,” is also grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ","chosen":"and, of prophecies, obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things","rationale":"This preserves the printed genitive προφητειῶν, both contrasted neuter expressions, the purpose clause, and ἀλλά without inserting an unattested predicate or extending the preceding negation. The resulting English remains syntactically fractured because the unchanged Greek does not provide a defensible continuous predication."},{"source_quote":"ἐνφύτῳ καὶ ἀεννάῳ πνεύματι","chosen":"through an innate and ever-flowing spirit","rationale":"The dative expresses the means by which the teacher knew. ἀένναος may also be rendered “unceasing,” “perpetual,” or “unfailing.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ οὐδενὸς δεῖται πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ","issue":"The image-checked selected reading is verified as printed, but no defensible continuous predication can be established. προφητειῶν is genitive plural, whereas ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα and ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ are nominative or accusative neuter plurals. A partitive or attributive relation between προφητειῶν and the first neuter expression is possible, but it does not supply the missing predicate. Ordinary ellipsis does not resolve the construction: neither ἐπίσταται nor ἐκτείνει yields a suitable meaning and case relation, while δεῖται governs the preceding οὐδενός and cannot govern the neuter forms as printed. The negative force of οὐδενός also cannot securely be extended across the following καί, and ἀλλά therefore lacks a defensibly recoverable contrasted predication. The context suggests that true foreknowledge does not deliver obscure and ambiguous predictions requiring another prophet’s interpretation but instead delivers explicit and plain ones; expressing that coherent sense would require wording not present in the selected reading. The translation consequently preserves the fracture, and the unresolved clause meaning blocks publication.","proposed_reading":"One possible but unverified conjecture is καὶ οὐδενὸς δεῖται πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, καὶ οὐ προφητεύει ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ (“and it needs no one for comprehension, and it does not prophesy obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things”). This conjecture replaces the printed προφητειῶν and supplies οὐ; it has not been substituted into the translation.","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
